knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The lesson asks learners to explain what they do and the kind of client they want, then ask one direct question. Asking for a purchase on the spot (option 0) and sending a price list with no conversation (option 2) are named mistakes.
The lesson requires the written agreement to cover referral handling, complaint handling and any reward. Logos (option 0) and follower counts (option 1) do not govern how referrals work.

The lesson says to follow a group's rule on pitching even when the service would help the room. Pitching anyway (option 1) and handing out cards regardless of the rules (option 2) both break the group rule.

practicalCriteria: Learner delivers a spoken introduction of 30 to 45 seconds that names who they help, the problem they solve and the referral they want.
Learner drafts a partnership agreement that covers referral handling, complaint handling and any reward, and lists any term left open for the partner to confirm.
Learner completes a warm-contact list with at least five contacts or groups, each with one specific request and a follow-up date.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Warm-contact list with requests and follow-up dates
Event or group attendance record showing the rules checked
stopWorkCriteria: Learner pitches at a group or event that forbids it
Learner accepts a referral for work outside the licence or insurance the business holds
Learner uses contact details collected at an event for a purpose the person did not agree to
